status: Lead-reviewed correction frozen before production implementation

scope.name: Same-connection rollback-journal write validation
scope.why: Smallest proposed repair with the current stdlib SQLite connection. It makes the already-observed SQLite moved-file write protection run before a read-only authority body can yield; it does not claim to read the descriptor or infer the connection from a pathname. Validate this mechanism in bounded fixtures before accepting it.
unchanged: Assigned fixture DB and original failed trees
guard_order: Retain existing signed enrollment, current path, exact connection UUID and database_list checks. Require the actual connection to be inside the owned outer transaction.

Require actual PRAGMA main.journal_mode to be exactly delete. Do not silently convert WAL, off, memory, persist, truncate or an unknown/malformed mode. These unsupported modes fail closed for enrolled authority paths; isolated unguarded Core fixtures remain available.

Before authority reads/yield, open one named internal SAVEPOINT on this exact connection; temporarily UPDATE the single store_identity row from its expected UUID to a fresh valid different UUID. Require exactly one matched row. This deliberate change avoids assuming that a no-op UPDATE will force a SQLite write.

ROLLBACK TO then RELEASE that savepoint; verify the original store UUID and repeat enrollment/path checks. Convert failure to validate/restore into AccessDenied and let the outer transaction roll back; do not continue on a partial check. This check is not a separately committed operation and issues no proof.

Use the same check at both existing transaction guard points, preserving prior outer task/outbox writes across the inner savepoint. Begin and guard remain before the work_boundary body. The precommit check is a last refusal boundary, not rollback of an already published external effect.
limits: This is proposed bounded SQLite write validation, not direct descriptor/inode attestation. The exact original ABA must refuse before the body on actual macOS and Linux SQLite runtimes; until then portability is unproven.

Only default rollback DELETE mode is proposed supported for enrolled authority. Other modes must explicitly refuse rather than inherit an untested guarantee. Adding support later requires its own actual moved-file proof.

The private store identity changes only inside an uncommitted savepoint and is restored before domain authority reads. Tests must prove unchanged committed identity, task/attempt/outbox/events/resources and stable replay. Guard I/O/journal overhead is a real tradeoff, bounded by one small indexed-row write/rollback per guard, twice per transaction.

Same-OS-user hostile replacement can coordinate repeated namespace swaps, overwrite data/keys or change the process. This is not an adversarial OS-user security boundary or a distributed lock. Trusted restoration still requires quiescence and owned state.

Cross-filesystem rename cannot be assumed atomic. The guard must refuse missing/replaced/mixed files without repairing them. SQLite itself documents that renaming active database files can lead to undefined/corrupt behavior; the fixture proves a refusal boundary for this fault, not support for live restore.

If the write validation does not reliably refuse the frozen read-only ABA before effect, do not stack pathname heuristics or weaken criteria. Escalate to a supported SQLite/VFS connection-bound mechanism and a separately reviewed portability/dependency change. No CPython object-offset/pointer hacks.

lead_review_additions: Generate a canonical valid UUID different from the enrolled expected UUID; generator exception/equality/malformed output refuses before UPDATE.
Temporary update is WHERE id=expected_uuid and must match exactly one row.
Any write, rollback, release or identity/path recheck failure aborts authority and preserves the outer transaction rollback.

controls.actions: Run original v9 four variants unchanged against baseline; retain the existing effect and moved-write results.
controls.expected: Historical failure remains the same evidence; no reinterpretation.

controls.actions: Run the exact open-copy/restore-original actual work_boundary sentinel on repaired DELETE guard, with diagnostic connection origin/UUID and original inode.
controls.expected: Typed refusal before body/effect; original human hold and both database domain facts unchanged.

controls.actions: Actual normal DELETE connection before/after a new task mutation and a committed same-key replay; include source/writing artifact expiry after the committed result.
controls.expected: Identity, tasks/outbox/attempt/resource effects are exact; no extra task/proof/provider effect, no policy reset; ordinary valid work still runs.

controls.actions: Actual WAL, OFF, MEMORY, PERSIST and TRUNCATE connections plus malformed/unknown mode query failure injection; attempt the same authority boundary.
controls.expected: All unsupported modes fail before temporary identity write/body/effect. Do not call a fabricated query result an actual SQLite mode.

controls.actions: Actual read-only URI connection and query_only connection, and an injected write/rollback/release I/O failure at each savepoint step.
controls.expected: Refusal before external effect; original identity restored by outer rollback/recovery. Setup/BEGIN refusal is recorded separately from a guard refusal.

controls.actions: Rename/source substitution before open, after BEGIN/before guard, between preliminary checks/write validation and before precommit. Include original restored ABA and missing path/cross-filesystem-failure injection.
controls.expected: Wrong connection or current namespace fails closed under the tested ordering; no canary is advertised as observing an OS descriptor. No automatic store adoption/recovery.

controls.actions: Owned subprocess crashes after temporary identity write, after savepoint rollback, and after a legitimate domain change before commit; reopen the enrolled original.
controls.expected: Actual SQLite rollback/recovery retains original identity and pretransaction domain facts; no competing ownership or accepted stale replay.

controls.actions: Two actual connections/processes: human hold wins before lease transaction; alternatively lease boundary holds BEGIN IMMEDIATE while a human writer waits, then completes and the hold commits.
controls.expected: When hold wins no effect; when lease wins exactly the bounded authorized effect, followed by hold/refusal for the next boundary. No stale-read interleaving over the same physical store.

controls.actions: Existing Task/claim/admission/reserve/start/readback/replay and installed CLI/MCP negatives on repaired source.
controls.expected: Original public schemas and command flow preserved; no new writer/selection/provider/model/human proof.

controls.actions: Run the frozen mechanism and normal-boundary controls on actual macOS and Linux runtime versions with retained hashes.
controls.expected: Record each platform separately. A missing Linux observation remains not_run, not portable acceptance.

production_gate: Actual private feasibility observed exact ABA refusal before body/effect on macOS SQLite3.50.4; normal valid DELETE worked. Linux evidence remains unrun. No full suite authorized.
